key_insight: An energy-structure-preserving finite element scheme provides mesh-independent stability for rotating MHD–Boussinesq flows with nonlinear power-law viscosity.
engineering_relevance: The scheme supports stable simulation of coupled flow, heat transfer, and magnetic effects in rotating electrically conducting fluids.
method: Conforming velocity and temperature elements, Nédélec magnetic elements, and semi-implicit backward Euler time stepping.
Exact Lorentz–induction energy cancellation and energy-neutral Coriolis forcing.
Time-translate compactness and a Minty argument for nonlinear diffusion identification.
evidence_signal: Three-dimensional numerical experiments confirm the predicted stability and convergence behaviour, alongside a priori error estimates requiring no mesh–time coupling.
watch_item: Genuine weak-solution identification is established for the Newtonian case and, in 3D, above a Lorentz-force-dependent exponent threshold—not throughout the shear-thickening regime.
paper_title: Finite Element Approximation of Rotating MHD-Boussinesq Flows with Nonlinear Power-Law Viscosity
